explanation: Tipping at UK restaurants is appreciated but discretionary, not obligatory. Many bills already include a 10-12.5% discretionary service charge, which can be removed if service was poor. Since 1 October 2024, the Employment (Allocation of Tips) Act 2023 requires employers to pass all tips and service charges to staff, so anything you leave goes directly to workers rather than the business.
local_tip: Check the bill for an already-added service charge before tipping extra; if there isn't one, 10-12.5% for good service is standard practice.

also_check.note: Tipping can be seen as insulting or confusing; excellent service is already the norm and included in the price.
Tipping 15-20% is expected and forms a major part of server income; not tipping is considered very rude.
Service is legally included in the bill ('service compris'), but rounding up or leaving small change for great service is a nice gesture.
